prompt: LAH opens an epoxide: 1,2-epoxybutane + LiAlH4; then H3O+. Draw the alcohol (H⁻ delivered to LESS hindered C).

answers.label: 2-butanol (hydride at terminal CH2 end, OH on 2°)

traps.note: H⁻ attacks the LESS substituted end — gives the MORE substituted alcohol.

explanation: LAH (hydride) is a Nu under basic conditions → SN2 attack at the less-hindered C. The 2° side keeps the alkoxide (then OH after workup). So reduction of a terminal epoxide with LAH gives the SECONDARY alcohol, not the primary. (DIBAL often gives the primary instead — different mechanism).
